events.title: Royal Canadian Circus
events.summary: The touring circus’s Burlington stop, with multiple daily shows over the Labour Day weekend.
events.details: Official tickets list Thursday 7:30 p.m.; Friday 4 and 7:30 p.m.; Saturday and Sunday 12, 4 and 7:30 p.m.; Monday 11 a.m. and 3 p.m. Doors open 30–45 minutes before showtime. Children 3 and under are free on an adult’s lap. Use the mall parking lot.
bring: A parking plan for Burlington Centre
events.imageAlt: The red-and-yellow Royal Canadian Circus big top at Burlington Centre.

events.title: Movies Under the Stars: Lilo & Stitch
events.dateLabel: Thu, Sept. 3 · 8 p.m. at Ireland Park
events.summary: The official City table also lists a September 3 screening at Ireland Park.
events.details: The City page intro says the series runs through August 27, but the published schedule table includes Thursday, September 3 at Ireland Park for Lilo & Stitch 2025. Confirm closer to the date.
bring: A weather check before you leave
events.imageAlt: Editorial reconstruction of a community outdoor movie night in a park.

events.title: Canada’s Largest Ribfest
events.summary: Four days of rib teams, music and fundraising on Burlington’s waterfront.
events.details: The festival runs 11 a.m. to 11 p.m. Friday through Sunday and 11 a.m. to 7 p.m. Monday. Food and drinks cost extra after admission.
bring: A plan for transit or parking
events.imageAlt: Ribs cooking over a barbecue pit
events.credit: Thogru via Wikimedia Commons · CC BY-SA 3.0

events.title: RBG After Dark: ANCHORBALL
events.summary: A 19+ evening walk through the ANCHORBALL sculptures with food, drinks and live entertainment.
events.details: Royal Botanical Gardens lists the remaining After Dark date as Sept. 5. Final entry is 9 p.m. Separate evening tickets are required. This is not the daytime garden admission.
bring: Photo ID if you look under 25
A payment card for food or drinks
events.imageAlt: Rock Garden at Royal Botanical Gardens
events.credit: Nhl4hamilton via Wikimedia Commons · public domain

events.title: BBCC BUMS Regatta and F18 Championships
events.summary: The Burlington Beach Catamaran Club’s annual BUMS regatta, including the F18 Canadian Championships.
events.details: A City of Burlington events memo lists the regatta and F18 championships at Beachway Park on Sept. 11–13, 2026. Spectator access and parking follow Beachway park rules. Exact start times can change with wind.
events.imageAlt: Burlington waterfront editorial visual. Not a photograph of this regatta.

events.title: Kerrfest
events.summary: Oakville’s Kerr Village festival with a Colin James and Jim Cuddy weekend.
events.details: This is a nearby Oakville festival, not a Burlington event. Visit Oakville lists Friday doors at 3:45 p.m., Saturday at 11:45 a.m. and Sunday kids programming from about 11 a.m. The Kerr Village BIA lineup names Colin James on Friday and the Jim Cuddy Band on Saturday. Confirm tickets and the Sunday schedule before you go.
bring: A warm layer for the evening sets
events.sourceName: Visit Oakville; Kerr Village BIA lineup
events.imageAlt: Neighbours outdoors in a local park. Editorial illustration.

events.title: Supercrawl
events.summary: A free weekend of music, art and street programming about 20 minutes from Burlington.
events.details: This is a nearby Hamilton pick, not a Burlington event. Check the official schedule before leaving because set times and road closures can change.
events.imageAlt: Illustrated collage used as a nearby-event visual

events.title: Burlington Asian Night Market
events.summary: A free weekend of Asian street food, vendors and night-market entertainment.
events.details: The organizer lists Friday 5 to 11 p.m., Saturday noon to 11 p.m. and Sunday noon to 9 p.m. Tourism Burlington also carries the weekend. Admission is listed as free. Food and shopping cost extra.
bring: A plan for parking at Mapleview
events.sourceName: Asian Night Market; listed by Tourism Burlington
events.imageAlt: Evening market food stalls. Editorial illustration.

events.title: Tiger-Cats vs. Montreal Alouettes
events.location: Hamilton Stadium, 64 Melrose Ave. N., Hamilton
events.summary: A Friday night CFL home game in Hamilton.
events.details: This is a nearby Hamilton sports date, not a Burlington event. Tourism Hamilton lists kickoff at 7:30 p.m. at Hamilton Stadium. Confirm tickets and gate times on the Tiger-Cats schedule before you leave.
events.imageAlt: Illustrated local sports collage

events.title: Salsa Saturdays at Pier 8
events.location: Pier 8 outdoor rink, 47 Discovery Drive, Hamilton
events.travel: About 25 minutes to the Hamilton waterfront
events.summary: A free sunset salsa lesson and dance on the Hamilton waterfront.
events.details: This is a nearby Hamilton event, not a Burlington event. The City of Hamilton lists a beginner lesson from 7 to 7:30 p.m. and dancing on the rink until 10:30 p.m. No ticket is required. Donations are appreciated. No partner or experience is needed.
bring: Comfortable shoes you can dance in
events.imageAlt: A public waterfront gathering place at dusk. Editorial visual, not Pier 8.

events.title: British Car Day at Bronte Creek
events.location: Bronte Creek Provincial Park, 1219 Burloak Drive, Oakville
events.travel: On the Burlington–Oakville line at Burloak Drive
events.summary: North America’s largest one-day all-British car show, with more than 1,000 cars.
events.details: This is a nearby Oakville park event, not a Burlington event. Spectators enter at 9 a.m. through the main Burloak gate. Ontario Parks charges a vehicle permit. Pedestrians and cyclists are free. Awards are at 2 p.m.
bring: Cash for the park gate if you can
events.imageAlt: Outdoor community gathering in a park. Editorial illustration.

events.title: Appleby Line Street Festival
events.location: Appleby Line between Fairview Street and New Street
events.summary: A free neighbourhood festival with vendors, food trucks, live music and a kid zone.
events.details: The City of Burlington lists almost 150 vendors, a food truck alley, live music and a kid zone. The event is free and community-led.
events.imageAlt: Street-level community event illustration

events.title: Baby-Sitters Club Canadian tour stop
events.location: Burlington Performing Arts Centre, 440 Locust Street
events.summary: Raina Telgemeier and Gale Galligan’s only Canadian stop on the Baby-sitters on Board! tour.
events.details: BPAC lists the show for ages 8 and up. Ticket-only is $20. Ticket plus book, signed bookplate and tote is $36. There is no book signing. Extra books will be sold in the lobby.
bring: No books from home for signing
events.imageAlt: Editorial illustration for a family theatre night. Not a tour photograph.

events.title: Milton Fall Fair
events.summary: The 171st Milton Fall Fair, with livestock, a midway and demolition derbies.
events.details: This is a nearby Milton fair, not a Burlington event. Official hours are Friday 3 to 11 p.m., Saturday 9 a.m. to 11 p.m. and Sunday 10 a.m. to 5 p.m. Gate prices and the derby schedule are on the fair site.
events.sourceName: Milton Fall Fair / Halton Agricultural Society
events.imageAlt: Fairground produce and late-summer market stalls. Editorial illustration.

events.title: Nickel Brook Beer Fest
events.summary: Third annual beer fest with craft pours, food trucks and live music. General-admission proceeds go to the Children’s Aid Foundation of Halton.
events.details: Eventbrite lists the 2026 date as Friday, Sept. 25, 6 to 11 p.m. Drink tokens are sold on site. A designated-driver ticket is available. This is the same evening as Patrick Watson at RBG.
events.imageAlt: Editorial food-and-crowd visual. Not a photograph of this beer fest.

events.title: Patrick Watson under the harvest moon
events.summary: An outdoor fall concert in the garden. General admission doors open at 5:30 p.m.
events.details: General admission seating is on the turf and chairs are not supplied. The event is outdoors and may be postponed, rescheduled or cancelled for weather.
events.imageAlt: Rock Garden at Royal Botanical Gardens
events.credit: Nhl4hamilton via Wikimedia Commons · public domain

events.title: Plant 500 native trees at Longmoor Park
events.summary: BurlingtonGreen and City forestry staff are planning a community planting morning.
events.details: The organizers plan to plant more than 500 native trees. Space is limited and registration was not yet open when this listing was checked.
events.imageAlt: Illustration of neighbours volunteering on a Burlington park path

events.title: Heritage Fibre Festival at Ireland House
events.summary: A pay-what-you-may Culture Days festival of spinning, weaving and historic-house demos.
events.details: Museums of Burlington lists live fibre demonstrations, a vendor market, children’s activities and local music at Ireland House, 2168 Guelph Line. Admission is pay-what-you-may. Pre-registration is not required.
bring: A bag if you shop the market
events.imageAlt: Illustrated Burlington history collage

events.title: Harvest Festival at Bronte Creek
events.location: Spruce Lane Farm, Bronte Creek Provincial Park, Oakville
events.travel: On the Burlington–Oakville line at Burloak Drive
events.summary: A two-day heritage harvest weekend with cider pressing, wagon rides and pumpkin picking.
events.details: This is a nearby Ontario Parks program, not a Burlington event. A valid park vehicle permit is required. Activities can change for weather. Tourism Burlington also lists the weekend.
bring: A park permit or cash for the gate
A bag if you pick a pumpkin
events.imageAlt: Harvest-season produce. Editorial illustration, not a Bronte Creek photo.

events.title: WANDER / Culture Days at BPAC
events.location: Burlington Performing Arts Centre, 440 Locust Street
events.summary: A free Culture Days walk through BPAC with pop-up performance and installations.
events.details: BPAC lists free drop-in admission between 1 and 4 p.m. as part of Culture Days and its 15th-anniversary season. The same Saturday also has the Heritage Fibre Festival at Ireland House.
events.imageAlt: Editorial public-art illustration for a Culture Days event.

events.title: Remembrance Day
events.location: Confirm the 2026 City ceremony location before you go
events.summary: Nov. 11 is Remembrance Day. The 2026 Burlington ceremony time and site had not been posted when this was checked.
events.details: The date is fixed. Do not treat a previous year’s cenotaph time as confirmed for 2026 until the City or the Royal Canadian Legion publishes it.
events.imageAlt: Editorial civic-gathering visual. Not a photograph of a 2026 ceremony.

events.title: Santa Claus Parade
events.location: Downtown Burlington · route to be confirmed for 2026
events.summary: The City has set Sunday, Dec. 6, 2026 as the parade date. The 2026 start time and route were not posted on the City page at last check.
events.details: The 2025 parade ran in the afternoon downtown. Do not assume the same clock time or route for 2026 until the City publishes them. Vendor applications open September 2026.
events.imageAlt: Editorial community-event visual. Not a photograph of the 2026 parade.
